narrative:
On July 29, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 42.2%, successfully hearing 1,041 out of 2,467 scheduled cases across 42 judge rosters. This reflects a performance recovery compared to the previous day’s rate of 39.5% (1,030 heard out of 2,610 scheduled) and the 36.9% rate recorded on July 24, though it remains below the recent peak of 44.7% achieved on July 27.

Performance varied significantly across court halls. H.P. Sandesh achieved strong disposal efficiency, hearing 61 out of 84 scheduled cases (72.6%), while Pradeep Singh Yerur and Vijaykumar A. Patil converted 69.1% (38 of 55) and 67.2% (39 of 58) of their dockets, respectively. Managing the single largest load of the day, S. Vishwajith Shetty heard 90 out of 250 scheduled matters (36.0%). Conversely, S. Rachaiah heard none of the 26 scheduled cases in Hall 26.

By procedural stage, cases listed for Orders saw the highest volume efficiency among major categories, converting 367 of 658 scheduled matters (55.8%), an improvement from 47.8% on July 28. Preliminary Hearings achieved a 42.5% hearing rate (180 of 424), while Final Hearings lagged at 23.8% (124 of 522). Across case types, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest portion of the docket with 1,113 scheduled matters, yielding 415 hearings (37.3%). Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) and Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) recorded clearance rates of 48.4% (182 of 376) and 47.0% (125 of 266), respectively, while Criminal Revision Petitions (CRL.RP) reached a high conversion rate of 73.4% (58 of 79).
